chunks: Al-Kafi: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from his father, from al-Nadhr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Ibn Muskan, from Zurara ibn A'yan, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, Allah is empty of His creations and His creations are empty of Him. And whatever falls under the name 'thing' is a creation, apart from Allah. And Allah is the Creator of all things. Blessed is He who is not like anything, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean that Allah is 'empty' of His creation in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the doctrine of divine transcendence (tanzih) by asserting that Allah is free from His creation and creation is free from Him, emphasizing that He is not composed of parts nor contained within them. The narration distinguishes all created entities as 'things' distinct from the Uncreated Creator, a concept central to Shia theological discourse on God's essence. It concludes by citing the Quranic verse affirming His unique perfection, reinforcing the principle that nothing in creation resembles the Divine.
